---
title: "Research"
subtitle: "Understanding animal movement to predict biodiversity futures"
description: "Research overview: animal dispersal, species distribution modelling, biodiversity forecasting, field technology and conservation applications using Bayesian methods and large-scale datasets."
---

Our research focuses on the ecological processes that drive the distribution and abundance of animal populations. We combine fieldwork, large-scale data synthesis (bird ringing, citizen science, camera traps) and quantitative modelling to tackle questions across spatial and temporal scales, and we try to make the results useful for conservation.

## Approach

Our work typically combines big datasets and quantitative methods:

- **Ring-recovery data** from EURING and national schemes, one of the largest individual-level animal movement datasets in the world
- **Citizen science observations**, especially eBird
- **Bayesian hierarchical models** implemented in R
- **Camera trapping and bioacoustic monitoring** in the field

We are committed to open science. Code and data for our papers are available on [GitHub](https://github.com/guifandos) and archived on [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/search?q=fandos).

## Collaborators

We work regularly with researchers at the University of Potsdam, the British Trust for Ornithology, the Swiss Ornithological Institute, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin and several Spanish institutions. See the [People](../people.html) page for the full list.
